title: Emission histogram and KV-influence instrumentation for per-token latency attribution
creator: Priya Raman
description: Add lightweight per-emission histograms and a KV-influence signal to the request tracing pipeline to enable accurate per-token latency and cost attribution without blowing up telemetry cardinality. This ticket implements: 1) an emission-level compact histogram (HDR-like) for sub-token timing distribution, 2) a compact representation of KV-cache hits/misses across emission positions, and 3) a backend aggregation job that merges histograms and attributes latency delta to cache behavior and batching effects. The goal is to produce actionable per-model and per-route metrics for: 99th/95th/median emission latencies, tail contribution by cache misses, and estimated token-level cost uplift attributable to cache penalty and repeated KV loads.
acceptance_criteria: Instrument runtime to emit an emission_histogram proto with at most one small (<=128 bytes) blob per response that represents per-subtoken timing distribution
Attach a KV_influence bitmask/summary (<=64 bits or compressed Bloom) that captures which emission positions observed KV hits vs misses

Aggregation pipeline consumes histograms and KV summaries and outputs per-model per-route metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, cache-miss-rate-by-position, and an estimated per-token cache penalty in ms and equivalent cost units
End-to-end overhead measured: <1.5% p50 latency increase when sampling at 100% for payloads under 128 tokens; disk/network telemetry budget increase accounted for in telemetry quotas
Dashboards with drill-down from request -> emission histogram -> cache-influence time series are available in Console and linked from the rollout
Documentation + SDK change (python/node) included and smoke-tested by infra e2e harness
technical_notes: Histogram encoding: use 17-bit compact HDR-style buckets serialized as base64 to keep payload small; fallback to sparse list for very short sequences
KV influence: represent as a 64-bit position mask for sequences <=64 tokens. For longer sequences emit a 64-bit sliding Bloom of positions (tunable hash seeds) to bound size
Trace fields: add micro_latency_ms (per-emission), emission_index, and kv_hit_summary fields to the existing tracing proto. Keep field additions backward-compatible and optional

Aggregation: stream histograms into the metrics pipeline (Kafka) and run a stateful aggregation job that merges histograms per (model,route,1m) and correlates with cache-hit summaries to compute delta distributions

Attribution model: compute expected latency if all positions were cache-hits by subtracting per-position cache-penalty estimated from aggregated samples. Convert ms to cost via our token-cost-per-ms lookup table to report cost uplift
Sampling strategy: default full sampling for internal traffic; 1% sampling for free-tier requests. Allow configuration per-customer and per-route via Console
Privacy/PII: histograms and masks contain no text/token content. Ensure we never include token strings in telemetry. Add review checklist for legal/compliance
Performance trade-offs: compact histograms add CPU to encode; Bloom approach trades false positives on position hits which biases the penalty down; document bias and include calibration job
implementation_steps: Spike: prototype runtime histogram encoder in runtime-shared library (done)
Change: add optional fields to trace proto and bump tracing lib (PR created)
Collector: update telemetry collector to accept base64 histogram and kv_summary (work in progress)
Aggregator: implement Kafka consumer aggregate job and unit tests
Console: add dashboard panels and drill-down links; wire metric names to rollout alerts
SDK: add helper to decode histograms in python and node clients
Rollout: canary under internal-only flag -> gradual enablement per-route -> public
testing_plan: Unit tests for histogram encode/decode covering edge cases (empty, single-bucket, long tail)
Integration test: runtime emits histogram & kv_summary, collector forwards to kafka, aggregator rebuilds p95/p99 within 2% of golden sample
Load test: run traffic at 2x baseline and validate <1.5% p50 latency increase when instrumentation enabled
A/B: short canary comparing customer route with and without instrumentation to validate no customer-visible regressions
Calibration: run controlled experiments toggling KV to force hits/misses and validate attribution model
dashboards: Console > Observability > Token Attribution > Model:{{model}} > p50/p95/p99 emission histogram
Console > Observability > Token Attribution > KV influence heatmap (position vs miss-rate)
Cost > Token Cost Uplift by Route > estimated_ms_uplift and estimated_usd_uplift

open_questions: What is the right default sampling rate for public customers to balance telemetry costs vs signal?
Do we accept Bloom false-positive bias for sequences >64 tokens or implement sharded masks at higher cost?
How should we expose estimated per-token cost uplift to customers without confusing billing? (dashboard vs billing API)
Should the aggregator store merged histograms for 90 days or summarize to precomputed percentiles after 7 days to save storage?
